Friday, December 20, 2019 
Title 3— 
The President 
Executive Order 13900 of December 17, 2019 
Providing for the Closing of Executive Departments and 
Agencies of the Federal Government on December 24, 2019 
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the 
laws of the United States of America, it is hereby ordered as follows: 
Section 1. All executive departments and agencies of the Federal Government 
shall be closed and their employees excused from duty on Tuesday, December 
24, 2019, the day before Christmas Day. 
Sec. 2. The heads of executive departments and agencies may determine 
that certain offices and installations of their organizations, or parts thereof, 
must remain open and that certain employees must report for duty on 
December 24, 2019, for reasons of national security, defense, or other public 
need. 
Sec. 3. December 24, 2019, shall be considered as falling within the scope 
of Executive Order 11582 of February 11, 1971, and of 5 U.S.C. 5546 and 
6103(b) and other similar statutes insofar as they relate to the pay and 
leave of employees of the United States. 
Sec. 4. The Director of the Office of Personnel Management shall take 
such actions as may be necessary to implement this order. 
Sec. 5. General Provisions. (a) This order shall be implemented consistent 
with applicable law and subject to the availability of appropriations. 
(b) Nothing in this order shall be construed to impair or otherwise affect: 
(i) the authority granted by law to an executive department or agency, 
or the head thereof; or 
(ii) the functions of the Director of the Office of Management and Budget 
relating to budgetary, administrative, or legislative proposals.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Section 1 closes all executive departments and agencies of the Federal Government and excuses their employees from duty on Tuesday, December 24, 2019 ("shall be closed and their employees excused from duty on Tuesday, December"). The text gives the reason as "the day before Christmas Day". The first end is the order's own terms with no later act needed: the order operates on Tuesday, December 24, 2019 only, and nothing in its text continues any command past December 24, 2019. The order has no effective-date wording of its own that postpones the day, so the end is recorded as the last day named, 2019-12-24, inclusive (the order runs through the end of that day); the alternative exclusive reading would end it when December 24, 2019 begins.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Section 4 directs the Director of the Office of Personnel Management to take such actions as may be necessary to implement the order ("such actions as may be necessary to implement this order."). It is an implementation command with no stated date and no held record of what the Director did or when. It implements only the closure and excusal for Tuesday, December 24, 2019, so it is read as having no operation after December 24, 2019; that reading is an inference from the order's text and is disclosed, and it does not rest on any completion date. The first end is the order's own terms with no later act needed: the order operates on Tuesday, December 24, 2019 only, and nothing in its text continues any command past December 24, 2019. The order has no effective-date wording of its own that postpones the day, so the end is recorded as the last day named, 2019-12-24, inclusive (the order runs through the end of that day); the alternative exclusive reading would end it when December 24, 2019 begins.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 13900, 84 FR 69983 (Federal Register Vol. 84, No. 245, Friday, December 20, 2019; filed December 19, 2019), signed December 17, 2019 (grade official_original_counted, machine text layer of the official PDF). The heading, number, title (Providing for the Closing of Executive Departments and Agencies of the Federal Government on December 24, 2019) and date agree with the census register. Text and inventory: I read the whole held text. It has sections 1 to 5 (section 5 with its sub-items), with no separate lead clause; the dossier's clause inventory matches those paragraphs and is complete. Lifecycle: the order closes the departments and agencies on Tuesday, December 24, 2019 and says nothing that runs past December 24, 2019, so every clause ends by the order's own terms on 2019-12-24 (section 5(d) excepted where it is dated separately). No later instrument names the order: the packet's lookup of held order texts for its number lists only its own Federal Register text, and the dossier's later-event chain is empty. The only other instrument the text names is Executive Order 11582 of February 11, 1971, an earlier order cited in section 3.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Own terms: the order closes the agencies on Tuesday, December 24, 2019 only (\"shall be closed and their employees excused from duty on Tuesday, December\") and states no other date or period. No later order is held that revokes, supersedes or amends it: the packet's lookup of held order texts for the number 13900 returned only the order's own Federal Register text, the later-events chain for this order has no entries, and the dossier's later-event search covers the Federal Register catalog's disposition notes from 1937 on. Executive Order 11582 (1971) is cited in section 3 as the pay-and-leave framework; it is earlier and is not an end. A report-deadline reading does not apply because the order has no report. Disclosed alternative: the exclusive reading would end the order when December 24, 2019 begins.","independent_command_check":"Independent commands: section 4 is the only command addressed to an officer other than the agencies' own heads (the Director of OPM); it implements the closure and has no separate subject, so it is not an independent continuing command. Sections 2 and 3 attach to the same closed day. Section 5 holds rules of construction and a no-rights statement, none of which creates a continuing duty.","savings_check":"Savings: the order contains no savings or continuing-effects wording other than its rules of construction. No clause is amended or ended in part by any held instrument, so the whole order ends with its last closed day."}

Presidential Documents
81337 
Federal Register 
Vol. 85, No. 242 
Wednesday, December 16, 2020 
Title 3— 
The President 
Executive Order 13965 of December 11, 2020 
Providing for the Closing of Executive Departments and 
Agencies of the Federal Government on December 24, 2020 
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the 
laws of the United States of America, it is hereby ordered as follows: 
Section 1. All executive departments and agencies of the Federal Government 
shall be closed and their employees excused from duty on Thursday, Decem-
ber 24, 2020, the day before Christmas Day. 
Sec. 2. The heads of executive departments and agencies may determine 
that certain offices and installations of their organizations, or parts thereof, 
must remain open and that certain employees must report for duty on 
December 24, 2020, for reasons of national security, defense, or other public 
need. 
Sec. 3. December 24, 2020, shall be considered as falling within the scope 
of Executive Order 11582 of February 11, 1971, and of 5 U.S.C. 5546 and 
6103(b) and other similar statutes insofar as they relate to the pay and 
leave of employees of the United States. 
Sec. 4. The Director of the Office of Personnel Management shall take 
such actions as may be necessary to implement this order. 
Sec. 5. General Provisions. (a) This order shall be implemented consistent 
with applicable law and subject to the availability of appropriations. 
(b) Nothing in this order shall be construed to impair or otherwise affect: 
(i) the authority granted by law to an executive department or agency, 
or the head thereof; or 
(ii) the functions of the Director of the Office of Management and Budget 
relating to budgetary, administrative, or legislative proposals.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Section 2 lets the heads of departments and agencies decide that certain offices and installations must remain open and that certain employees must report for duty on the closed day, for reasons of national security, defense, or other public need ("December 24, 2020, for reasons of national security, defense, or other public"). It is a discretion that attaches to the closure in section 1 and has no operation once the closed day is over. The first end is the order's own terms with no later act needed: the order operates on Thursday, December 24, 2020 only, and nothing in its text continues any command past December 24, 2020. The order has no effective-date wording of its own that postpones the day, so the end is recorded as the last day named, 2020-12-24, inclusive (the order runs through the end of that day); the alternative exclusive reading would end it when December 24, 2020 begins.

The pay and leave consequences for the closed day are recorded under savings. The first end is the order's own terms with no later act needed: the order operates on Thursday, December 24, 2020 only, and nothing in its text continues any command past December 24, 2020. The order has no effective-date wording of its own that postpones the day, so the end is recorded as the last day named, 2020-12-24, inclusive (the order runs through the end of that day); the alternative exclusive reading would end it when December 24, 2020 begins.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Section 4 directs the Director of the Office of Personnel Management to take such actions as may be necessary to implement the order ("such actions as may be necessary to implement this order."). It is an implementation command with no stated date and no held record of what the Director did or when. It implements only the closure and excusal for Thursday, December 24, 2020, so it is read as having no operation after December 24, 2020; that reading is an inference from the order's text and is disclosed, and it does not rest on any completion date. The first end is the order's own terms with no later act needed: the order operates on Thursday, December 24, 2020 only, and nothing in its text continues any command past December 24, 2020. The order has no effective-date wording of its own that postpones the day, so the end is recorded as the last day named, 2020-12-24, inclusive (the order runs through the end of that day); the alternative exclusive reading would end it when December 24, 2020 begins.

Title 3—

Executive Order 13965 of December 11, 2020 
Providing for the Closing of Executive Departments and 
Agencies of the Federal Government on December 24, 2020 
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the 
laws of the United States of America, it is hereby ordered as follows: 
Section 1. All executive departments and agencies of the Federal Government 
shall be closed and their employees excused from duty on Thursday, Decem-
ber 24, 2020, the day before Christmas Day. 
Sec. 2. The heads of executive departments and agencies may determine 
that certain offices and installations of their organizations, or parts thereof, 
must remain open and that certain employees must report for duty on 
December 24, 2020, for reasons of national security, defense, or other public 
need. 
Sec. 3. December 24, 2020, shall be considered as falling within the scope 
of Executive Order 11582 of February 11, 1971, and of 5 U.S.C. 5546 and 
6103(b) and other similar statutes insofar as they relate to the pay and 
leave of employees of the United States. 
Sec. 4. The Director of the Office of Personnel Management shall take 
such actions as may be necessary to implement this order. 
Sec. 5. General Provisions. (a) This order shall be implemented consistent 
with applicable law and subject to the availability of appropriations. 
(b) Nothing in this order shall be construed to impair or otherwise affect: 
(i) the authority granted by law to an executive department or agency, 
or the head thereof; or 
(ii) the functions of the Director of the Office of Management and Budget 
relating to budgetary, administrative, or legislative proposals.

Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 13965, 85 FR 81337 (Federal Register Vol. 85, No. 242, Wednesday, December 16, 2020; filed December 15, 2020), signed December 11, 2020 (grade official_original_counted, machine text layer of the official PDF). The heading, number, title (Providing for the Closing of Executive Departments and Agencies of the Federal Government on December 24, 2020) and date agree with the census register. Text and inventory: I read the whole held text. It has sections 1 to 5 (section 5 with its sub-items), with no separate lead clause; the dossier's clause inventory matches those paragraphs and is complete. Lifecycle: the order closes the departments and agencies on Thursday, December 24, 2020 and says nothing that runs past December 24, 2020, so every clause ends by the order's own terms on 2020-12-24 (section 5(d) excepted where it is dated separately). No later instrument names the order: the packet's lookup of held order texts for its number lists only its own Federal Register text, and the dossier's later-event chain is empty. The only other instrument the text names is Executive Order 11582 of February 11, 1971, an earlier order cited in section 3.

Executive Order 13983 of January 19, 2021 
Revocation of Executive Order 13770 
By the authority vested in me as President of the United States by the 
Constitution and laws of the United States of America, including section 
301 of title 3, United States Code, and sections 3301 and 7301 of title 
5, United States Code, it is hereby ordered as follows: 
Section 1. Revocation. Executive Order 13770 of January 28, 2017, ‘‘Ethics 
Commitments by Executive Branch Appointees,’’ is hereby revoked, effective 
at noon January 20, 2021. Employees and former employees subject to the 
commitments in Executive Order 13770 will not be subject to those commit-
ments after noon January 20, 2021. 
Sec. 2. General Provisions. (a) Nothing in this order shall be construed 
to impair or otherwise affect: 
(i) the authority granted by law to an executive department or agency, 
or the head thereof; or 
(ii) the functions of the Director of the Office of Management and Budget 
relating to budgetary, administrative, or legislative proposals. 
(b) This order shall be implemented consistent with applicable law and 
subject to the availability of appropriations. 
(c) This order is not intended to, and does not, create any right or benefit, 
substantive or procedural, enforceable at law or in equity by any party 
against the United States, its departments, agencies, or entities, its officers, 
employees, or agents, or any other person. 
THE WHITE HOUSE, 
January 19, 2021.

Filed 1–22–21; 8:45 am]

Presidential Documents
6835 Federal Register / Vol. 86, No. 14 / Monday, January 25, 2021 / Presidential Documents 
Executive Order 13983 of January 19, 2021 
Revocation of Executive Order 13770 
By the authority vested in me as President of the United States by the 
Constitution and laws of the United States of America, including section 
301 of title 3, United States Code, and sections 3301 and 7301 of title 
5, United States Code, it is hereby ordered as follows: 
Section 1. Revocation. Executive Order 13770 of January 28, 2017, ‘‘Ethics 
Commitments by Executive Branch Appointees,’’ is hereby revoked, effective 
at noon January 20, 2021. Employees and former employees subject to the 
commitments in Executive Order 13770 will not be subject to those commit-
ments after noon January 20, 2021. 
Sec. 2. General Provisions. (a) Nothing in this order shall be construed 
to impair or otherwise affect: 
(i) the authority granted by law to an executive department or agency, 
or the head thereof; or 
(ii) the functions of the Director of the Office of Management and Budget 
relating to budgetary, administrative, or legislative proposals. 
(b) This order shall be implemented consistent with applicable law and 
subject to the availability of appropriations. 
(c) This order is not intended to, and does not, create any right or benefit, 
substantive or procedural, enforceable at law or in equity by any party 
against the United States, its departments, agencies, or entities, its officers, 
employees, or agents, or any other person. 
THE WHITE HOUSE, 
January 19, 2021.

Filed 1–22–21; 8:45 am]

Title 3— 
The President 
Executive Order 14129 of December 18, 2024 
Providing for the Closing of Executive Departments and 
Agencies of the Federal Government on December 24, 2024 
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the 
laws of the United States of America, it is hereby ordered as follows: 
Section 1. All executive departments and agencies of the Federal Government 
shall be closed and their employees excused from duty on Tuesday, December 
24, 2024, the day before Christmas Day. 
Sec. 2. The heads of executive departments and agencies may determine 
that certain offices and installations of their organizations, or parts thereof, 
must remain open and that certain employees must report for duty on 
December 24, 2024, for reasons of national security, defense, or other public 
need. 
Sec. 3. December 24, 2024, shall be considered as falling within the scope 
of Executive Order 11582 of February 11, 1971, and of 5 U.S.C. 5546 and 
6103(b) and other similar statutes insofar as they relate to the pay and 
leave of employees of the United States. 
Sec. 4. The Director of the Office of Personnel Management shall take 
such actions as may be necessary to implement this order. 
Sec. 5. General Provisions. (a) Nothing in this order shall be construed 
to impair or otherwise affect: 
(i) the authority granted by law to an executive department or agency, 
or the head thereof; or 
(ii) the functions of the Director of the Office of Management and Budget 
relating to budgetary, administrative, or legislative proposals. 
(b) This order shall be implemented consistent with applicable law and 
subject to the availability of appropriations.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Section 1 closes all executive departments and agencies of the Federal Government and excuses their employees from duty on Tuesday, December 24, 2024 ("shall be closed and their employees excused from duty on Tuesday, December"). The text gives the reason as "the day before Christmas Day". The first end is the order's own terms with no later act needed: the order operates on Tuesday, December 24, 2024 only, and nothing in its text continues any command past December 24, 2024. The order has no effective-date wording of its own that postpones the day, so the end is recorded as the last day named, 2024-12-24, inclusive (the order runs through the end of that day); the alternative exclusive reading would end it when December 24, 2024 begins.

187 Federal Register / Vol. 90, No. 2 / Friday, January 3, 2025 / Presidential Documents 
Executive Order 14133 of December 30, 2024 
Providing for the Closing of Executive Departments and 
Agencies of the Federal Government on January 9, 2025 
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the 
laws of the United States of America, it is hereby ordered as follows: 
Section 1. All executive departments and agencies of the Federal Government 
shall be closed on January 9, 2025, as a mark of respect for James Earl 
Carter, Jr., the thirty-ninth President of the United States. 
Sec. 2. The heads of executive departments and agencies may determine 
that certain offices and installations of their organizations, or parts thereof, 
must remain open and that certain employees must report for duty on 
January 9, 2025, for reasons of national security, defense, or other public 
need. 
Sec. 3. January 9, 2025, shall be considered as falling within the scope 
of Executive Order 11582 of February 11, 1971, and of 5 U.S.C. 5546 and 
6103(b) and other similar statutes insofar as they relate to the pay and 
leave of employees of the United States. 
Sec. 4. The Director of the Office of Personnel Management shall take 
such actions as may be necessary to implement this order. 
Sec. 5. General Provisions. (a) Nothing in this order shall be construed 
to impair or otherwise affect: 
(i) the authority granted by law to an executive department or agency, 
or the head thereof; or 
(ii) the functions of the Director of the Office of Management and Budget 
relating to budgetary, administrative, or legislative proposals. 
(b) This order shall be implemented consistent with applicable law and 
subject to the availability of appropriations.

Presidential Documents
40227 Federal Register / Vol. 90, No. 158 / Tuesday, August 19, 2025 / Presidential Documents 
Executive Order 14337 of August 13, 2025 
Revocation of Executive Order on Competition 
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the 
laws of the United States of America, it is hereby ordered: 
Section 1. Revocation. Executive Order 14036 of July 9, 2021 (Promoting 
Competition in the American Economy), is hereby revoked. 
Sec. 2. General Provisions. (a) Nothing in this order shall be construed 
to impair or otherwise affect: 
(i) the authority granted by law to an executive department or agency, 
or the head thereof; or 
(ii) the functions of the Director of the Office of Management and Budget 
relating to budgetary, administrative, or legislative proposals. 
(b) This order shall be implemented consistent with applicable law and 
subject to the availability of appropriations. 
(c) This order is not intended to, and does not, create any right or benefit, 
substantive or procedural, enforceable at law or in equity by any party 
against the United States, its departments, agencies, or entities, its officers, 
employees, or agents, or any other person. 
(d) The costs for publication of this order shall be borne by the Department 
of Justice. 
THE WHITE HOUSE, 
August 13, 2025.

Filed 8–18–25; 8:45 am]

Executive Order 14371 of December 18, 2025 
Providing for the Closing of Executive Departments and 
Agencies of the Federal Government on December 24, 2025, 
and December 26, 2025 
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the 
laws of the United States of America, it is hereby ordered: 
Section 1. All executive departments and agencies of the Federal Government 
shall be closed and their employees excused from duty on Wednesday, 
December 24, 2025, and Friday, December 26, 2025, the day before and 
the day following Christmas Day, respectively. 
Sec. 2. The heads of executive departments and agencies may determine 
that certain offices and installations of their organizations, or parts thereof, 
must remain open and that certain employees must report for duty on 
December 24, 2025, or December 26, 2025, or both, for reasons of national 
security, defense, or other public need. 
Sec. 3. December 24, 2025, and December 26, 2025, shall be considered 
as falling within the scope of Executive Order 11582 of February 11, 1971, 
and of 5 U.S.C. 5546 and 6103(b) and other similar statutes insofar as 
they relate to the pay and leave of employees of the United States. 
Sec. 4. The Director of the Office of Personnel Management shall take 
such actions as may be necessary to implement this order. 
Sec. 5. General Provisions. (a) Nothing in this order shall be construed 
to impair or otherwise affect: 
(i) the authority granted by law to an executive department or agency, 
or the head thereof; or 
(ii) the functions of the Director of the Office of Management and Budget 
relating to budgetary, administrative, or legislative proposals.

Presidential Documents
60545 Federal Register / Vol. 90, No. 244 / Tuesday, December 23, 2025 / Presidential Documents 
Executive Order 14371 of December 18, 2025 
Providing for the Closing of Executive Departments and 
Agencies of the Federal Government on December 24, 2025, 
and December 26, 2025 
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the 
laws of the United States of America, it is hereby ordered: 
Section 1. All executive departments and agencies of the Federal Government 
shall be closed and their employees excused from duty on Wednesday, 
December 24, 2025, and Friday, December 26, 2025, the day before and 
the day following Christmas Day, respectively. 
Sec. 2. The heads of executive departments and agencies may determine 
that certain offices and installations of their organizations, or parts thereof, 
must remain open and that certain employees must report for duty on 
December 24, 2025, or December 26, 2025, or both, for reasons of national 
security, defense, or other public need. 
Sec. 3. December 24, 2025, and December 26, 2025, shall be considered 
as falling within the scope of Executive Order 11582 of February 11, 1971, 
and of 5 U.S.C. 5546 and 6103(b) and other similar statutes insofar as 
they relate to the pay and leave of employees of the United States. 
Sec. 4. The Director of the Office of Personnel Management shall take 
such actions as may be necessary to implement this order. 
Sec. 5. General Provisions. (a) Nothing in this order shall be construed 
to impair or otherwise affect: 
(i) the authority granted by law to an executive department or agency, 
or the head thereof; or 
(ii) the functions of the Director of the Office of Management and Budget 
relating to budgetary, administrative, or legislative proposals. 
(b) This order shall be implemented consistent with applicable law and 
subject to the availability of appropriations. 
(c) This order is not intended to, and does not, create any right or benefit, 
substantive or procedural, enforceable at law or in equity by any party 
against the United States, its departments, agencies, or entities, its officers, 
employees, or agents, or any other person.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Section 4 directs the Director of the Office of Personnel Management to take such actions as may be necessary to implement the order ("such actions as may be necessary to implement this order."). It is an implementation command with no stated date and no held record of what the Director did or when. It implements only the closure and excusal for Wednesday, December 24, 2025, and Friday, December 26, 2025, so it is read as having no operation after December 26, 2025; that reading is an inference from the order's text and is disclosed, and it does not rest on any completion date. The first end is the order's own terms with no later act needed: the order operates on Wednesday, December 24, 2025, and Friday, December 26, 2025 only, and nothing in its text continues any command past December 26, 2025. The order has no effective-date wording of its own that postpones the day, so the end is recorded as the last day named, 2025-12-26, inclusive (the order runs through the end of that day); the alternative exclusive reading would end it when December 26, 2025 begins.

Presidential Documents
60545 Federal Register / Vol. 90, No. 244 / Tuesday, December 23, 2025 / Presidential Documents 
Executive Order 14371 of December 18, 2025 
Providing for the Closing of Executive Departments and 
Agencies of the Federal Government on December 24, 2025, 
and December 26, 2025 
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the 
laws of the United States of America, it is hereby ordered: 
Section 1. All executive departments and agencies of the Federal Government 
shall be closed and their employees excused from duty on Wednesday, 
December 24, 2025, and Friday, December 26, 2025, the day before and 
the day following Christmas Day, respectively. 
Sec. 2. The heads of executive departments and agencies may determine 
that certain offices and installations of their organizations, or parts thereof, 
must remain open and that certain employees must report for duty on 
December 24, 2025, or December 26, 2025, or both, for reasons of national 
security, defense, or other public need. 
Sec. 3. December 24, 2025, and December 26, 2025, shall be considered 
as falling within the scope of Executive Order 11582 of February 11, 1971, 
and of 5 U.S.C. 5546 and 6103(b) and other similar statutes insofar as 
they relate to the pay and leave of employees of the United States. 
Sec. 4. The Director of the Office of Personnel Management shall take 
such actions as may be necessary to implement this order. 
Sec. 5. General Provisions. (a) Nothing in this order shall be construed 
to impair or otherwise affect: 
(i) the authority granted by law to an executive department or agency, 
or the head thereof; or 
(ii) the functions of the Director of the Office of Management and Budget 
relating to budgetary, administrative, or legislative proposals. 
(b) This order shall be implemented consistent with applicable law and 
subject to the availability of appropriations. 
(c) This order is not intended to, and does not, create any right or benefit, 
substantive or procedural, enforceable at law or in equity by any party 
against the United States, its departments, agencies, or entities, its officers, 
employees, or agents, or any other person.

It ends before the closed days do, and the whole-order end stays 2025-12-26.

The heading, number, title (Providing for the Closing of Executive Departments and Agencies of the Federal Government on December 24, 2025, and December 26, 2025) and date agree with the census register. Text and inventory: I read the whole held text. It has sections 1 to 5 (section 5 with its sub-items), a lead paragraph and section 5(d) on publication costs; the dossier's clause inventory matches those paragraphs and is complete. Lifecycle: the order closes the departments and agencies on Wednesday, December 24, 2025, and Friday, December 26, 2025 and says nothing that runs past December 26, 2025, so every clause ends by the order's own terms on 2025-12-26 (section 5(d) excepted where it is dated separately). No later instrument names the order: the packet's lookup of held order texts for its number lists only its own Federal Register text, and the dossier's later-event chain is empty. The only other instrument the text names is Executive Order 11582 of February 11, 1971, an earlier order cited in section 3.

Executive Order 14371 of December 18, 2025 
Providing for the Closing of Executive Departments and 
Agencies of the Federal Government on December 24, 2025, 
and December 26, 2025 
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the 
laws of the United States of America, it is hereby ordered: 
Section 1. All executive departments and agencies of the Federal Government 
shall be closed and their employees excused from duty on Wednesday, 
December 24, 2025, and Friday, December 26, 2025, the day before and 
the day following Christmas Day, respectively. 
Sec. 2. The heads of executive departments and agencies may determine 
that certain offices and installations of their organizations, or parts thereof, 
must remain open and that certain employees must report for duty on 
December 24, 2025, or December 26, 2025, or both, for reasons of national 
security, defense, or other public need. 
Sec. 3. December 24, 2025, and December 26, 2025, shall be considered 
as falling within the scope of Executive Order 11582 of February 11, 1971, 
and of 5 U.S.C. 5546 and 6103(b) and other similar statutes insofar as 
they relate to the pay and leave of employees of the United States. 
Sec. 4. The Director of the Office of Personnel Management shall take 
such actions as may be necessary to implement this order. 
Sec. 5. General Provisions. (a) Nothing in this order shall be construed 
to impair or otherwise affect: 
(i) the authority granted by law to an executive department or agency, 
or the head thereof; or 
(ii) the functions of the Director of the Office of Management and Budget 
relating to budgetary, administrative, or legislative proposals. 
(b) This order shall be implemented consistent with applicable law and 
subject to the availability of appropriations. 
(c) This order is not intended to, and does not, create any right or benefit, 
substantive or procedural, enforceable at law or in equity by any party 
against the United States, its departments, agencies, or entities, its officers, 
employees, or agents, or any other person.
